solution.brief: Wasp multi-part aggregation: combining multiple distinct part types with different connection configurations in a single aggregation
solution.principle:
Related insight: Related insight: Tutorial 07 (wasp_07) advances beyond the multi-part aggregation foundation established here into more complex aggregation techniques. The multi-part pattern (managing independent connection index spaces per part type, cross-part rules, distinct connection configurations) is a direct prerequisite for the advanced aggregation workflows introduced in tutorial 07.

Related insight: Related insight: The multi-part aggregation foundation established here feeds into an extended tutorial series that now reaches tutorial 15 (wasp_15), covering increasingly advanced modular and rules-based discrete assembly workflows.

Related insight: Related insight: Graph-grammar-based aggregation (as in wasp_graph_grammar_aggregation_setup) is an alternative to stochastic aggregation for multi-part setups with directional connections and attributes. The same foundational part-definition pattern — two or more part types, independent connection index spaces, attribute-driven rules — applies to both stochastic and graph-grammar aggregation engines. Learners familiar with multi-part stochastic aggregation can transfer this knowledge directly to graph-grammar workflows.

intents: create a stochastic aggregation with Wasp
set up Wasp basic part with attributes
use Wasp to aggregate geometry with connection rules
build a Wasp assembly with custom attributes

evolution_history.changes: wasp_07 is tagged as advancing beyond the multi-part basics; wasp_06_multi_part is the direct conceptual predecessor and should be marked as a prerequisite and extended with advanced context.

wasp_06 is a foundational tutorial whose techniques propagate through the entire series. Adding 'modular' and 'rules-based' tags and noting the series extent to tutorial 15 keeps this pattern's context current and discoverable.

The new pattern uses the same multi-part, attribute-driven, connection-configured setup but with a graph-grammar aggregation engine. This expands the neighbor's context to acknowledge graph-grammar as a parallel aggregation approach and adds the relevant tag.

curriculum.title: Build Part
curriculum.text:
1. Build Part
Parts are the building blocks of Wasp.
The most basic way of initializing a part is to define t he geometry (as brep or mesh),
and the connection faces (center and orientation - with a line). Parts must be named
to be identifyed in the aggregation rules.

curriculum.title: Part Attributes
curriculum.text:
2. Part Attributes
It is possible to define an unlimited number of attributes,
which are associated to the part and carried along during
aggregation.
Attributes can be both geometric or non-geometric types.
In the case of non-geometric types, the TR input must
be set to False (as the attributes cannot be transformed).

NB: a large amount or complex geometric attributes will slow
down the aggregation process. In the case of very complex
geometries, the Part Replacement approach is more suitable
and less computationally expensive.
(see example file: 0_04_Part_Geometry_Replacement).

curriculum.title: Extract Attributes
curriculum.text:
4. Extract Attributes
Attributes can be retrieved from a specific part
using their ID. The resulting values can be used
for further Grasshopper processing.
